history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and multiple strokes
vision loss in the right eye
persistent symptoms for 1.5 years
visual acuity ranging between 20/100 to 20/200
severe macular changes with associated edema
persistent central macular thickness of 669.8 [79.3] μm
over 12 visits
changes in macular edema over the course of treatment

concepts.why: The patient's severe macular changes with associated edema, persistent central macular thickness, and changes in macular edema over the course of treatment support this diagnosis.
The patient's vision loss and severe macular changes, combined with the mention of reversible effect on cystoid macular edema secondary to retinal vein occlusion, support this diagnosis.
The patient's changes in macular edema over the course of treatment, specifically after stopping niacin therapy, support this diagnosis.
The patient's vision loss and decreased visual acuity, combined with a history of hypertension and multiple strokes, support this diagnosis.
The patient's severe macular changes with associated edema and persistent central macular thickness support this diagnosis, although the absence of explicit diabetes diagnosis makes it less likely.
The patient's history of hypertension and vision loss support this diagnosis, although the presence of other retinal conditions makes it less likely.
The patient's severe macular changes with associated edema and the mention of reversible effect on cystoid macular edema secondary to retinal vein occlusion support this diagnosis.
The patient's severe macular changes with associated edema and the mention of reversible effect on cystoid macular edema secondary to retinal vein occlusion support this diagnosis.

The patient's severe macular changes with associated edema and persistent central macular thickness support this diagnosis, although the absence of explicit age-related macular degeneration diagnosis makes it less likely.

The patient's vision loss and decreased visual acuity, combined with a history of hypertension and multiple strokes, support this diagnosis, although the presence of other retinal conditions makes it less likely.
It explains the changes in macular edema under different treatment conditions, specifically after stopping Niacin therapy.

rationales.F06: Severe macular changes with associated edema are highly suggestive of Cystoid Macular Edema.
rationales.F07: Persistent central macular thickness of 669.8 μm is a strong indicator of Cystoid Macular Edema.
rationales.F10: The reversible effect on Cystoid Macular Edema secondary to Retinal Vein Occlusion after stopping Niacin therapy is a strong indicator of Niacin-Induced Macular Edema.
